headline: Six of seven majors above their 200-day line, but today's ETF print and whale flow both lean the other way
paragraphs: Start with the regime, because it's lopsided in a way that matters: BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, BNB, and DOGE all sit above their 200-day moving averages with golden crosses confirmed on four of them. Only ADA trades below its 200-day, despite being up 41.7% on the month. That's a market where the trend structure is broadly intact, not a coin flip. Bitcoin itself is still 37.2% below its 12-month high of $124,739.81, so 'above the 200-day' here means recovering, not euphoric.

Momentum is where the first wrinkle shows. Every asset's RSI-14 sits in the high 50s to high 60s, healthy but not overbought, and that's consistent with the price action: BTC is down 0.9% on the day, up a token 0.2% on the week, and up 23.1% on the month. But MACD has gone bearish (below signal) on BTC, ETH, and SOL even as their 200-day trend holds bullish. That's a real divergence: trend says up, the shorter momentum gauge says the thrust has faded. BNB, DOGE, and ADA still show MACD above signal, so the group isn't uniform, but the two largest coins by cap are the ones cooling off first.

Positioning adds texture rather than alarm. BTC funding on OKX is 0.0063% per 8 hours (6.9% annualized), modest cost for longs, with a long/short ratio of 1.2 and open interest at $2.15B. That's leveraged, but not stretched: liquidations in the last 2 hours ran $774K longs versus $111K shorts, meaning longs are the ones getting flushed on dips, a sign of crowding on the bull side without a full unwind. SOL and XRP funding have actually flipped negative (-1.6% and -2.2% annualized), meaning shorts are paying longs to hold their bets there, an unusual posture for coins still up double digits on the month.

Flows are where the day's tension sharpens. BTC spot ETFs printed a net outflow of $46.6M on 08 Sep 2026, the same day XRP and BNB were green and BTC itself was red. But the five-session window shows a net inflow of $723.4M, and same_direction_days sits at just 1, so today's outflow interrupts rather than confirms any run. ETH ETFs show the identical shape: an outflow of $24.3M on the day against a five-session net inflow of $103.4M. Whale wallets echo the daily caution: $317.3M net moved onto exchanges in the last 24 hours, with BTC alone contributing $251.7M onto exchanges (much of it into Coinbase and Coinbase Institutional) and ETH adding $65.6M more. Zoom out to the weekly ledger and the pattern isn't new: three of the last four weekly windows (Aug 19, Aug 26, and the week ending Sep 09 at $564M) show net flow onto exchanges, broken only by a $158M net outflow in the week ending Sep 02. Stablecoin float, meanwhile, is up 1.42% over 30 days to $310.4B, dry powder building even as coins move toward exchanges rather than away from them.

Sentiment sits at 66, Greed, near the top of its own 30-day range of 27 to 74. That's the crowd feeling good about a tape that, today specifically, shows ETF redemptions and whales pushing coins onto exchanges, both of which are more consistent with distribution than accumulation on this particular day. The five-session ETF numbers and the broader trend structure don't share that caution, which is exactly the kind of disagreement worth sitting with rather than resolving.

Worth watching from here: whether BTC's MACD crosses back above signal (trend and momentum realigning) or whether the divergence deepens into a 200-day test; whether tomorrow's ETF print returns to inflow or extends today's outflow into a same-direction run; and whether the weekly whale ledger's next entry breaks the onto-exchanges pattern the way the Sep 02 week briefly did.
